<description>
**Problem:** Overlapping `scantxoutset` calls can leave the node reporting "Scan already in progress" until restart, even though the scan has finished. A new caller can acquire the reservation while progress from the previous scan is still nonzero. The progress check then throws before the caller records that it owns the reservation, so its destructor never releases it.

**Fix:** Reset progress while the finishing scan still holds the reservation.

**Historical context:** [Luke pointed out](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/19362#discussion_r463934011) that a failed progress check could block all future scans.
</description>

ACK 5043b75e01c50b4b3fef3f332e46f401ee7b0a97

The reordering fixes the race described. If a new caller's `g_scan_in_progress.exchange(true)` reads the `false` stored by the finishing scan, it is guaranteed to also see the earlier `g_scan_progress = 0`. The only code that writes `g_scan_progress` is `FindScriptPubKey` and the destructor, and both run while holding the reservation. So after this change the `CHECK_NONFATAL(g_scan_progress == 0)` in `reserve()` holds.

The trigger is more common than the description suggests. `status` and `abort` call `reserve()` as well, so they also run the `CHECK_NONFATAL`. A second `start` is not needed. A client polling `scantxoutset` status in a loop, which is the documented way to follow a long scan, can hit the window right as the scan finishes. It then gets an "Internal bug detected" error, and from that point every `start` fails with "Scan already in progress" until the node restarts. This makes the bug much more likely to be hit in practice.

Non-blocking suggestion: the reservation may still leak if the check ever fails for some other reason, because `reserve()` throws before it sets `m_could_reserve`. Setting the flag before the check would make that case recover on its own:

```C++
if (g_scan_in_progress.exchange(true)) {
    return false;
}
m_could_reserve = true;
CHECK_NONFATAL(g_scan_progress == 0);
return true;
```
</new_statements>
